title_en: Chunyang Village Villagers Committee v. Huanan Gold Mine Bureau — dispute over compensation for damage to paddy fields caused by pollution from gold mining dredges

full_text_en:
Chunyang Village Villagers' Committee v. Huanan Gold Mine Bureau — Dispute over Compensation for Damage to Paddy Fields Caused by Pollution from Gold Dredge Discharge

Plaintiff: Chunyang Village Villagers' Committee, Shitouhezi Town, Huanan County, Heilongjiang Province (hereinafter referred to as "Chunyang Village").

Legal Representative: Ren Fuzhi, Director of Chunyang Village Villagers' Committee.

Agents ad litem: Wang Zhibin, Secretary of the Party Branch of Chunyang Village; Chen Shengjun, Accountant of Chunyang Village Villagers' Committee.

Defendant: Huanan Gold Mine Bureau of the Ministry of Metallurgical Industry (hereinafter referred to as the "Gold Mine Bureau").

Legal Representative: Zhu Xingkuan, Deputy Director of the Gold Mine Bureau.

Agents ad litem: Kong Fanyi, Section Chief of the Enterprise Management Section of the Gold Mine Bureau; (another agent ad litem) Deputy Section Chief of the Environmental Protection Section of the Gold Mine Bureau.

Plaintiff Chunyang Village filed a lawsuit with the Huanan County People's Court of Heilongjiang Province, seeking compensation for damage to paddy fields caused by pollution from the Defendant Gold Mine Bureau's gold mining discharge. The court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a public hearing on November 6, 1987, and found the following facts:

In 1978, the Defendant constructed Gold Dredge No. 1025 on the upper reaches of Liu Shu River in Shitouhezi Town, Huanan County. After the dredge commenced operation, it was discovered that the water flow of Liu Shu River was not concentrated and was unsuitable for dredge production. In June 1982, without approval from relevant authorities, the Defendant arbitrarily cut off the Liu Shu River, raised the water level, and diverted river water into the No. 1025 dredge pond via an artificial canal of 700 meters. The artificial canal was constructed of mine soil. During dredge operation, wastewater was discharged directly into the lower reaches of Liu Shu River without any treatment, causing the suspended solids in the river water to increase from the original 143 mg/L to 5,558 mg/L. At the water intake of Chunyang Village's paddy fields, the suspended solids reached 3,318 mg/L, exceeding the national maximum allowable discharge standard of 500 mg/L for industrial wastewater by 2,818 mg/L.

On-site investigation revealed that out of 824 mu of paddy fields in Chunyang Village, 162.3 mu were polluted, resulting in a yield reduction of 58.3 kg per mu, an annual reduction of 9,462.1 kg, and a total reduction of 37,848.4 kg over four years. Calculated at RMB 0.50 per kg of grain, the total loss amounted to RMB 18,924.2. Due to the large amount of mud slurry discharged by the No. 1025 dredge pond into Liu Shu River, the main irrigation channel for 100.63 mu of paddy fields in Chunyang Village was inundated with silt and required cleaning. The deepest silt accumulation in the paddy fields reached 39 cm, with an average depth of 12.2 cm. The annual silt removal volume was 8,184 cubic meters, totaling 32,736 cubic meters over four years. At a cost of RMB 1 per cubic meter for silt removal, the total labor cost was RMB 32,736. To transport this silt by truck, with a daily trucking cost of RMB 15 and a daily transport volume of 15 cubic meters, the total cost was RMB 32,736. The silt accumulation in the main canal, branch canals, and river barrage amounted to 1,038.31 cubic meters, requiring cleaning twice a year. Over four years, 8,306.48 cubic meters of silt needed to be removed. After deducting 15.07% for natural pollution and the state-permitted discharge volume of 1,252 cubic meters, Chunyang Village had to remove 7,115.8 cubic meters of silt, requiring 705.5 person-days of labor. At a labor cost of RMB 5 per person-day, the total labor cost was RMB 3,528.

The Huanan County People's Court held that, according to Article 5, Paragraph 1 of the Water Pollution Prevention and Control Law of the People's Republic of China, "all units and individuals have the responsibility to protect the water environment"; Article 29 stipulates that "industrial wastewater and urban sewage discharged into farmland irrigation channels shall ensure that the water quality at the nearest downstream irrigation water intake point complies with the water quality standards for farmland irrigation." Article 29 of the Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China (Trial Implementation) provides that "the discharge of wastewater must meet national standards." However, the Huanan Gold Mine Bureau of the Ministry of Metallurgical Industry, without approval from any authority, diverted the Liu Shu River and introduced river water into the dredge pond. During the operation of Gold Dredge No. 1025, no preventive measures were taken. The dredge used river water to wash gold and then discharged severely超标 tailings water directly into the Liu Shu River, causing large amounts of tailings water containing suspended solids to flow downstream, resulting in the blockage of Chunyang Village's irrigation channels, pollution of paddy fields, and reduction of rice yields. The Defendant shall bear direct responsibility for the water pollution. The Plaintiff, in accordance with Article 124 of the General Principles of Civil Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 41, Paragraph 1 of the Water Pollution Prevention and Control Law, requested that the Defendant bear civil liability and compensate for losses. This request should be supported.

In conclusion, the Huanan County People's Court rendered the following judgment on November 20, 1987:

The Plaintiff's rice production reduction over four years was 37,848.4 kg, calculated at RMB 0.50 per kg, totaling a loss of RMB 18,924.2; the loss of labor costs and trucking costs for removing silt from polluted paddy fields over four years totaled RMB 65,472; the loss for removing silt from the main canal, branch canals, and river barrage over four years totaled RMB 3,528. The total loss suffered by the Plaintiff over four years was RMB 87,924.2, which shall be compensated by the Defendant, payable in a lump sum upon the effectiveness of this judgment.

Litigation costs of first instance: RMB 2,029, to be borne by the Defendant.

The Defendant, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Jiamusi Intermediate People's Court. The grounds for appeal were: acknowledging that it should bear certain responsibility for exceeding the standard discharge during gold mining, but arguing that it should not bear all of the Plaintiff's losses, only those losses after deducting the reduction in production and labor costs caused by other factors.

Upon second-instance trial, the Jiamusi Intermediate People's Court held that the first-instance court had fully considered the reasons raised by the appellant. In calculating the losses, it had already deducted 15.07% for natural pollution and the state-permitted discharge volume, as well as the silt area of less than 3 cm. The facts found by the first-instance court were clear, the rights and wrongs and responsibilities were clearly defined, and the applicable law was correct. The appellant's grounds for appeal were not supported. In accordance with Article 151, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Trial Implementation), the court rendered a judgment on January 30, 1988, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

Litigation costs of second instance: RMB 2,026, to be borne by the appellant.
